author: Mecso
quote:
Literally only GTA in name. We waited years for a life Sim with all the fun parts stripped out. Tons of glitches and bugs, poor frame rate dropping down to 20/15 FPS in some areas. Many of the things we all wanted to do have all been removed. This was supposed to be the game of the generation. AAA gaming in the west is actually dead. Truly insane this was what they gave us after 13 years. Disappointment doesn't even begin to describe it. Trying to get a refund but they have made that impossible so I'm uninstalling the game and freeing up hard drive space. 
Rockstar completely dropped the ball here.

author: Mecso
quote:
Reclaiming the Crown: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2)
​Remaking what is widely regarded as one of the greatest video games of all time is a daunting gamble. Deliver a carbon copy, and it feels redundant; change too much, and you risk alienating generations of devoted fans. The Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time walks this tightrope with astounding confidence, resulting not just in a nostalgic tribute, but in a complete reimagining that feels modern, vibrant, and essential.
​Visual Splendor: Hyrule Like You’ve Never Seen It
​From the moment you step out of Kokiri Forest onto Hyrule Field, the leap in graphical fidelity is breathtaking. The Switch 2 hardware flexes its muscle here: sweeping vistas bathed in volumetric sunlight, lush fields of grass reacting realistically to wind and footfalls, and water shaders in Lake Hylia that make the original look like a distant memory.
​Character models manage to stay faithful to Yusuke Nakano’s iconic original art style while integrating subtle micro-expressions, cloth physics, and high-resolution textures. Lighting in dungeons—particularly the eerie glow of the Shadow Temple and the subterranean gloom of the Fire Temple—transforms classic locations into atmospheric showpieces. It looks phenomenal, capturing how our childhood imaginations remembered it looking rather than how it actually did in 1998.
​Re-engineered Gameplay: Fluid, Tactile, and Modern
​Where this remake truly earns its stripes is in how it plays. While the fundamental bones remain the same, nearly every control interaction has been refreshed for modern standards:
​Fluid Controls & Free Camera: The era of wrestling with rigid camera angles is finally gone. Full, intuitive 360-degree camera control pairs with silky-smooth 60 FPS movement and combat responsiveness.
​Streamlined UI & Item Swapping: The tedious menu-hopping of old is replaced by an intuitive radial wheel and dedicated utility buttons—making iron boots and weapon switches effortless.
​Revamped Combat Dynamics: The pioneering Z-targeting system feels sharper and more visceral, supported by subtle haptic feedback that makes every sword parry, shield block, and spin attack intensely tactile.
​Puzzles retain their original brilliance, but modernized environmental physics give your toolkit—from the Hookshot to the Megaton Hammer—a weight and responsiveness that make every dungeon encounter deeply satisfying.
​A Narrative Masterpiece, Preserved and Elevated
​Narratively, Ocarina of Time was already near perfection, and the remake treats its story with the reverence it deserves. The tragic dichotomy between Link's innocent childhood and the post-apocalyptic, Ganondorf-ruled future carries more emotional weight than ever.
​Cinematics have been re-directed with subtle, cinematic flair, letting the atmospheric score and expressive faces tell the story without disrupting the original pacing. The musical arrangements—re-orchestrated with rich acoustic instrumentation while retaining Koji Kondo’s timeless melodies—deliver goosebumps in every corner of the map.

​The Verdict
​This isn't merely an upscale; it is a masterclass in how to reimagine a foundational classic for a new generation. Fresh, gorgeous, and mechanically fluid, the Switch 2 edition proves that Ocarina of Time’s core is eternal, providing both lifelong fans and newcomers with an unforgettable adventure.
